articles.title: Servidor é flagrado espiando mulheres em banheiro de unidade de saúde no PI | G1
articles.standfirst: Imagens mostram homem olhando por cima de uma porta e se abaixando para tentar enxergar pelas frestas. Prefeita de Pimenteiras determinou abertura de processo administrativo para apurar o caso.
articles.summary: Imagens mostram homem olhando por cima de uma porta e se abaixando para tentar enxergar pelas frestas. Prefeita de Pimenteiras determinou abertura de processo administrativo para a
articles.body:
Um servidor de uma unidade de saúde de Pimenteiras , no Sul do Piauí, foi flagrado espiando mulheres no banheiro do estabelecimento. Um vídeo gravado no local mostra o homem olhando pelas frestas de uma porta.

Após tomar conhecimento da denúncia, a prefeita de Pimenteiras, Lúcia Lacerda, determinou a abertura de um Processo Administrativo Disciplinar (PAD) para apurar a conduta do servidor. Em nota, a gestora informou que pediu ao secretário municipal de Saúde que adotasse as medidas administrativas necessárias para a investigação.

"As mulheres têm o direito de utilizar qualquer espaço público com tranquilidade, privacidade e dignidade. Nenhuma mulher deve se sentir constrangida, ameaçada ou desrespeitada", disse a gestora.

Momento em que servidor é supostamente flagrado espiando mulheres — Foto: Reprodução

Leia a íntegra da nota da Prefeitura de Pimenteiras

Como prefeita de Pimenteiras e Presidente do Conselho da Mulher Municipalista da APPM, venho manifestar meu profundo repúdio a qualquer atitude que represente desrespeito, constrangimento, violência ou violação da intimidade e da dignidade das mulheres.

Ao tomar conhecimento de denúncia envolvendo um servidor municipal de uma Unidade Básica de Saúde do nosso município, relacionada a uma suposta conduta de violar a intimidade de mulheres, determinei imediatamente ao Secretário Municipal de Saúde que adotasse as medidas administrativas necessárias para a abertura do Processo Administrativo Disciplinar, a fim de que os fatos sejam devidamente apurados.

Esclarecemos que não toleramos comportamento dessa natureza em nenhum espaço público, principalmente um ambiente de saúde, que deve ser um lugar de acolhimento, segurança e respeito.

As mulheres têm o direito de utilizar qualquer espaço público com tranquilidade, privacidade e dignidade. Nenhuma mulher deve se sentir constrangida, ameaçada ou desrespeitada. Como gestora pública e defensora dos direitos das mulheres, tenho o dever de agir, proteger e garantir que situações dessa natureza sejam tratadas com a seriedade que merecem.

A apuração seguirá os procedimentos legais, assegurando o direito de defesa e o devido processo legal, garantindo atenção e respeito às mulheres envolvidas. Pimenteiras é uma cidade que cuida, protege, respeita e garante a dignidade de todas as mulheres.

articles.title: Tentativa de homicídio em Tarabai: suspeito é preso após agressão | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima de 28 anos foi socorrida inconsciente com hemorragia facial grave e transferida para o Hospital Regional de Presidente Prudente (SP). Caso será investigado.
articles.summary: Tentativa de homicídio em Tarabai deixou a vítima de 28 anos com hemorragia facial grave; o agressor foi localizado pela PM e o caso segue sob investigação policial.
articles.body:
Polícia Civil de Tarabai (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/Polícia Civil

Um homem de 26 anos foi preso na tarde deste domingo (1º) suspeito de espancar uma pessoa em frente a um mercado no Centro de Tarabai (SP).

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, a Polícia Militar foi acionada por volta das 11h40 após denúncias de que uma pessoa estava sendo agredida na rua Tiradentes.

Ao chegarem ao local, os policiais encontraram a vítima, de 28 anos, caída desacordada no chão e com um sangramento intenso no rosto. Inicialmente, a vítima foi socorrida por uma ambulância e encaminhada ao Pronto-Socorro de Pirapozinho (SP).

No entanto, devido à gravidade dos ferimentos, precisou ser transferido para a Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) do Hospital Regional (HR) de Presidente Prudente (SP) onde, até a última atualização desta reportagem, seguia internado.

O suspeito foi localizado pela equipe policial próximo ao local onde o crime aconteceu. Ainda segundo o boletim de ocorrência, ele possuía passagem na polícia. O caso foi registrado como tentativa de homicídio na Polícia Civil de Tarabai e será investigado.

articles.title: Abastecimento de água em Sergipe é afetado por obras em adutora | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Iguá Sergipe, intervenção na Adutora do Semiárido continua por conta da alta complexidade técnica. Caminhões-pipa atendem serviços essenciais.
articles.summary: O abastecimento de água em Sergipe sofre interrupções em diversos municípios devido a uma manutenção complexa na Adutora do Semiárido realizada pela Iguá Sergipe.
articles.body:
Torneira sem água. — Foto: Pedro França/Agência Senado/Arquivo

Uma intervenção programada para melhorias na Adutora do Semiárido tem provocado impactos temporários no fornecimento de água de municípios sergipanos. A informação foi confirmada, neste domingo (1º), pela concessionária Iguá Sergipe.

Segundo a empresa, os serviços tiveram início na última quinta-feira (29) e continuam em andamento devido à alta complexidade técnica dos trabalhos. Para diminuir os efeitos na região do semiárido, foram realizadas manobras no sistema de abastecimento neste domingo, o que redistribui o fornecimento e afeta temporariamente novas localidades.

O impacto no abastecimento foi dividido entre as áreas afetadas pelas manobras operacionais e as atingidas diretamente pelas obras na adutora.

A partir deste domingo (1º), as manobras no sistema afetam temporariamente os municípios de Canhoba, Cumbe, Feira Nova, Graccho Cardoso, Itabi, Nossa Senhora de Lourdes e povoados do município de Gararu.

Já as obras de melhoria na Adutora do Semiárido causam desabastecimento ou oscilações nos municípios de Carira, Frei Paulo, Nossa Senhora Aparecida, Nossa Senhora da Glória, Pedra Mole, Pinhão, Porto da Folha, Ribeirópolis e São Miguel do Aleixo, além da zona rural de Feira Nova .

Para minimizar os transtornos durante o período de manutenção, a concessionária informou que disponibiliza caminhões-pipa direcionados ao atendimento emergencial de serviços essenciais, como escolas e unidades de saúde.

Em nota, a Iguá Sergipe lamentou os transtornos e ressaltou que a intervenção é fundamental para garantir a segurança e a melhoria do sistema de abastecimento a longo prazo. A população pode buscar atendimento por meio dos canais oficiais da concessionária.

articles.title: How will the Iran war shape the outcome of the US midterm vote?
articles.summary: The conflict has become a central issue ahead of Tuesday’s polls.
articles.body:
The war on Iran has emerged as a major campaign issue in the United States midterm elections.

Voters are preparing to cast their ballots on Tuesday, November 3, and for many, the effects of the Iran conflict at home are top of mind.

Fuel prices have skyrocketed, driving up the prices of other goods, too.

Polls suggest many Democrats – and Republicans – say this conflict was not worth the consequences.

So will the election shift the Senate and House of Representatives in Democrats’ favour? And what would that mean for the rest of President Donald Trump’s time in the White House?

articles.title: Dia de Finados tem missas em cemitérios e esquema de trânsito especial em João Pessoa | G1

articles.summary: A segurança será reforçada nos cemitérios para assegurar a tranquilidade durante o período de visitação.
articles.body:
Dia de Finados tem missas em cemitérios de João Pessoa — Foto: Francisco França/Jornal da Paraíba

O Dia de Finados terá programação de missas em cemitérios de João Pessoa nesta segunda-feira (2). O esquema também conta com segurança reforçada da Guarda Civil Metropolitana (GCM) e da Polícia Militar para assegurar a tranquilidade durante o período de visitação.

A Prefeitura Municipal se João Pessoa estima que mais de 40 mil pessoas visitem os cemitérios da capital paraibana no feriado.

Os cemitérios públicos, administrados pela Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Urbano (Sedurb), estarão abertos à visitação das 6h às 18h (confira a programação de cada um deles abaixo) .

Cemitério Senhor da Boa Sentença (Varadouro)

7h e 9h – Missas celebradas pelo Padre Manoel

11h – Missa com o Arcebispo da Paraíba, Dom Delson

16h – Missa com o Padre Wancelei Cunha de Oliveira

Cemitério Santa Catarina (Bairro dos Estados)

9h e 16h – Missas com o Padre Mário Costa Silva

16h – Missa celebrada pelo Padre Luiz Júnior

As missas serão realizadas na Comunidade Cristã São Francisco, em frente ao Cemitério do Cristo, na Rua Presidente Nereu Ramos, N° 1.414.

Esquema de trânsito para o Dia de Finados

De acordo com a Superintendência Executiva de Mobilidade Urbana de João Pessoa (Semob-JP) , um planejamento para o trânsito no dia de Finados vai ser feito, a partir das 6h, no entorno dos seguintes cemitérios:

No cemitério da Boa Sentença vai haver o bloqueio do tráfego em frente ao cemitério. Veículos serão desviados pela Avenida Sanhauá e ruas próximas, com rotas alternativas para Bayeux e Ilha do Bispo.

No cemitério São José vai haver o bloqueio total da Avenida Cruz das Armas, em frente ao cemitério. O sentido Centro-bairro será desviado pelas ruas Santos Coelho e Porfírio Costa.

Já no cemitério do Cristo, haverá bloqueios nas ruas Heronides Vieira, Morise de Miranda Gusmão, dos Milagres, do Jarro e Olívia Almeida Guerra para garantir o acesso seguro ao cemitério.

Em relação ao Parque das Acácias, a Semob-JP informou que vai ter monitoramento do trânsito no entorno do cemitério pelos agentes de mobilidade.

No cemitério Santa Catarina há um bloqueio em frente ao cemitério, no cruzamento da Avenida Santa Catarina com a Avenida Espírito Santo. As linhas de ônibus 504 e 1001 terão seus itinerários desviados por ruas próximas.

No dia de Finados, as linhas do transporte coletivo urbano vão circular em João Pessoa com quadro de domingos, com um reforço de 10 veículos nas 54 linhas à disposição da população. Ao todo, serão 142 ônibus urbanos em operação realizando 894 viagens.

A Semob-JP também informou que além da frota para os cemitérios, as linhas 109, 204, 116, 401, 110, 107, 602, 120 e as circulares 1500 e 5100 vão ser reforçadas para atender funcionários dos shoppings centers, restaurantes, como também para quem for às praias.

articles.title: Cursinho da Unesp de Prudente faz aulão para o Enem; confira | G1
articles.standfirst: Atividades serão realizadas nos dias 7 e 14 de novembro, com transmissão ao vivo pelo YouTube; 260 vagas presenciais em Presidente Prudente (SP) já foram preenchidas.
articles.summary: O Cursinho Ideal da Unesp de Presidente Prudente promove um aulão de revisão para o Enem 2026, nos dias 7 e 14 de novembro, com transmissão ao vivo gratuitamente.
articles.body:
Cursinho da Unesp de Presidente Prudente faz aulão para o Enem — Foto: Reprodução/Unesp de Presidente Prudente

O Cursinho Ideal da Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp), em Presidente Prudente (SP), promove um aulão de revisão para o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) 2026, nos dias 7 e 14 de novembro.

As atividades serão realizadas durante todo o dia, às vésperas das provas. As 260 vagas para participação presencial já foram preenchidas, mas os interessados poderão acompanhar as aulas gratuitamente pelo canal da FCT-Unesp no YouTube .

A iniciativa, intitulada 1º Aulão Ideal Enem 2026, tem como objetivo ampliar a preparação dos estudantes para o exame e apresentar à comunidade o trabalho desenvolvido pelo cursinho popular.

As atividades serão realizadas no Auditório da FCT-Unesp, em dois sábados. No dia 7 de novembro, a programação será voltada aos conteúdos de Redação, Linguagens e Ciências Humanas.

Pela manhã, serão realizadas revisões de Inglês, Gramática, Literatura e Redação. À tarde, os estudantes terão aulas de História, Geografia, Filosofia e Sociologia.

Já no dia 14 de novembro, o foco será nas áreas de Ciências da Natureza e Matemática.

A programação começará com uma roda de conversa conduzida pela psicóloga Grazielle Setti. Em seguida, serão realizadas revisões de Matemática e Física, pela manhã, e Biologia e Química, à tarde.

Nos dois dias, os participantes que assistirem às aulas presencialmente também terão coffee break e atividades de karaokê durante os intervalos.

O evento conta com apoio da Pró-Reitoria de Extensão Universitária e Cultura (Proec) da Unesp e da Rede Nacional de Cursinhos Populares (Cpop).

Cursinho da Unesp de Presidente Prudente faz aulão para o Enem com transmissão ao vivo — Foto: Reprodução/Unesp de Presidente Prudente

Além das atividades educacionais, o aulão terá uma ação solidária para arrecadar alimentos não perecíveis.

Os mantimentos arrecadados serão destinados ao Fundo Social de Solidariedade de Presidente Prudente.

articles.title: Justiça determina que Águas do Pará restabeleça serviço em Belém | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão liminar atende a pedido da Prefeitura após atraso em manutenção. Concessionária afirma que ainda não foi notificada e que serviço foi restabelecido no sábado (31).
articles.summary: Decisão liminar atende a pedido da Prefeitura após atraso em manutenção. Concessionária afirma que ainda não foi notificada e que serviço foi restabelecido no sábado (31).
articles.body:
Vários bairros da capital paraense ficaram sem água durante o fim de semana. — Foto: Pedro França/Agência Senado

A Justiça do Pará determinou, na manhã deste domingo (1º), que a concessionária Águas do Pará adote medidas emergenciais imediatas para restabelecer o fornecimento de água e garantir transparência sobre a pane no sistema que afeta Belém .

A decisão atende a um pedido apresentado pela Procuradoria-Geral do Município (PGM) na noite de sábado (31), após moradores de cerca de 20 bairros relatarem falta de água durante o fim de semana.

O impasse começou após uma manutenção programada pela concessionária, prevista inicialmente para ocorrer entre as 20h de sexta-feira (30) e as 5h de sábado (31), em cinco bairros. O serviço, no entanto, deixou vários bairros de Belém desabastecidos.

A Prefeitura de Belém recorreu à Justiça alegando que a demora e a falta de informações claras prejudicaram a população.

Em nota enviada ao g1 , a Águas do Pará informou que ainda não foi notificada da decisão judicial e afirmou que o abastecimento já foi totalmente normalizado em todos os bairros afetados desde o fim da tarde de sábado (31) (leia o posicionamento completo abaixo).

A decisão, realizada pela juíza Diana Cristina Ferreira da Cunha, determina um cronograma que deve ser cumprido pela Águas do Pará sob pena de multas:

Em até 2 horas: Apresentar relatório técnico detalhado por bairro e divulgar em canais oficiais a lista de áreas afetadas e pontos de distribuição de água (com atualização a cada seis horas).

Em até 6 horas: Garantir fornecimento emergencial por caminhões-pipa, priorizando hospitais, postos de saúde, abrigos e pessoas acamadas.

Em até 12 horas: Comprovar nos autos as ações realizadas, detalhando rotas e volume de água distribuído.

Em nota, a concessionária explicou que a interrupção no fornecimento foi necessária para a realização de uma "intervenção de alta complexidade técnica" na rede de distribuição localizada no bairro da Condor.

Segundo a empresa, os trabalhos começaram às 20h de sexta-feira (30) e foram concluídos às 17h de sábado (31), mobilizando uma equipe de 33 profissionais.

A Águas do Pará informou que o abastecimento já está normalizada nos seguintes bairros: Comércio, Campina, Cidade Velha, Reduto, Batista Campos, Jurunas, Umarizal, Nazaré, Guamá, Cremação, Condor, São Brás, Fátima, Terra Firme, Canudos e partes da Pedreira e do Marco.

A empresa informou ainda que, durante a paralisação, manteve o atendimento emergencial com caminhões-pipa prioritariamente para serviços essenciais, lamentou os transtornos e reforçou que segue em diálogo com a Prefeitura e com a Agência de Regulação e Controle dos Serviços Públicos do Estado (Arcon).

articles.title: Trump administration's social media posts ahead of elections criticized for being inflammatory
articles.summary: The Trump administration’s online accounts are circulating images of a pumpkin carved with a sombrero design and a fake Halloween-themed background around a...
articles.body:
The Trump administration's online accounts are circulating images of a pumpkin carved with a sombrero design and a fake Halloween-themed background around a Black man apparently accused of food assistance fraud, in social media posts slammed by critics as inflammatory rhetoric.

Only days before the midterm elections, the posts coincide with the government's sweeping campaign to show its aggressive immigration enforcement , and highlight efforts to crack down on fraud to save taxpayers money when rising healthcare costs and other economic stressors have made affordability a top voter concern.

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins posted Saturday on the social platform X a photo of the Black man standing in front of stacks of what appear to be U.S. currency with the headline, SNAP FRAUDSTER, an apparent reference to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, formerly known as food stamps.

He is holding aloft what appears to be a bill set aflame.

"Some costumes come with a price tag. This one comes with a prison sentence," it says to the backdrop of fake Spirit Halloween costume packaging.

Another photo posted by the White House on X on Thursday showed a pumpkin with the shape of a sombrero carved across it and the words "Spooky szn is here."

The post by Rollins, who was nominated by Trump to serve as the U.S. Secretary of Agriculture in November 2024, appears to be taken from an Instagram post from September 2025 by an account under the name Shawty Dred.

Earlier this month, Mercedes Reshard New, identified by the Justice Department as a social media personality also known as "Shawty Dred," was arrested on federal charges for fraudulently obtaining more than $4 million in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits in Georgia.

It's not the first time the White House has been accused of posting inflammatory images on official government social media accounts.

Just over a year ago during the government shutdown, the White House revived a deepfake video posted by Trump of House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries in a fake mustache and sombrero to accuse the Democrats of acting on behalf of illegal immigrants instead of U.S. citizens. Jeffries described the meme as bigoted. They played it on repeat in the White House briefing room, though Vice President JD Vance promised that the "sombrero memes will stop" when Democrats agreed to end the shutdown.

The NAACP did not respond to an email seeking comment, nor did the White House or Rollins.

The Trump administration in recent weeks has ratcheted up its anti-immigrant rhetoric and accusations of fraud, including against U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar whose Washington, D.C., home was searched by federal agents earlier this month. Federal authorities are investigating potential fraud in her family's immigration paperwork. Omar, who was born in Somalia, is a naturalized U.S. citizen.

It also has taken a series of punitive steps linked to allegations of fraud in mostly Democratic-led states , including California and Minnesota whose governors accused the federal government of targeting their states for political reasons.

Federal prosecutors said in a news release Oct. 21 that the influencer, New, controlled more than 350 fraudulent SNAP accounts under stolen identities between January 2020 and July 2026. He allegedly applied for his company, Shawty Dred LLC, to become an authorized SNAP retailer and used EBT debit cards to extract about $4 million from the accounts.

New's Instagram account, which has more than two million followers, has flaunted his extravagant lifestyle, federal prosecutors said. Posts depict him flying on private jets, posing with Rolls-Royce vehicles in front of his "super mansion," and handling massive stacks of cash.

"Instead of this money feeding families in need, New, the social media personality known as 'Shawty Dred,' allegedly used the cash to bankroll a life of luxury," Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta Marlo Graham said in the release.

New was indicted by a federal grand jury Oct. 7 on dozens of counts of mail fraud and aggravated identity theft, and one count each of SNAP fraud and illegal transactions with access devices. He was arrested Oct. 13 and remains in federal custody.

According to Fulton County jail records, New has been arrested multiple times on suspicion of crimes including identity theft, insurance fraud, financial transaction card fraud, forgery and simple assault.

A federal defender listed in court records as representing New, Joseph Austin, did not return a phone message.

articles.title: 'Squad' rakes in record $2.35M while slamming the door on cop donations
articles.summary: The Squad Victory Fund raised a record $2.35 million this cycle while explicitly barring donations from the Fraternal Order of Police union.
articles.body:
A joint fundraising committee for four progressive House Democrats has raised a record $2.35 million so far this election cycle, while barring donations from the Fraternal Order of Police, according to federal filings and the committee's disclosure.

The Squad Victory Fund is authorized by Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez , D-N.Y.; Ilhan Omar, D-Minn.; Ayanna Pressley, D-Mass.; and Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich. The fundraising gives the four lawmakers and their allied political groups a shared vehicle to collect and distribute campaign contributions.

The fund's donor rules also make clear which groups it says it will not accept money from, and one is the Fraternal Order of Police, the nation's largest police organization. It also bars donations from corporations, federal lobbyists and fossil fuel interests. The disclosure does not explain the FOP exclusion.

The fund's other participants include four allied PACs. Contributions are generally divided equally among the eight participants, with each slated to receive 12.5%, though donors may designate their contributions for a specific participant.

The fund has raised $2,351,388.02 in the 2025–2026 election cycle, its highest total to date, according to its FEC summary.

Through March 31, 2026, it had spent about $1.6 million and reported roughly $68,000 in cash on hand. The committee remains active, so those figures may change.

Contributions are not tax-deductible, the disclosure notes.

images.caption: Split photo of Talib, Omar, and AOC.
"Squad" members of Congress Tlaib, Omar and Ocasio-Cortez.
The Squad Victory Fund says it will not accept contributions from the Fraternal Order of Police, the nation's largest police organization.

articles.title: Trump says he’ll become ‘Mr. Veto’ if Democrats take Congress
articles.summary: President Trump said his strategy if the GOP loses control of the House and Senate would be to “become Mr. Veto.” “Well, if that happens, I guess I’ll become Mr. Veto. I’m not going to let them through,” Trump told the New York Post’s Miranda Devine during an interview on “Pod Force One” set to…
articles.body:
President Trump said his strategy if the GOP loses control of the House and Senate would be to “become Mr. Veto.”

“Well, if that happens, I guess I’ll become Mr. Veto. I’m not going to let them through,” Trump told the New York Post’s Miranda Devine during an interview on “Pod Force One” set to air Monday.

“And then at some point, we’ll probably make deals. That’s what’s happened to me. This wouldn’t be the first time you’ll have a president, and he won’t have the House or the Senate.”

“They’ll be sending stuff up. You veto it, and eventually, after a month or two of getting all vetoed,” the president continued. “Take them over and you make a deal. I think that probably would happen, but hopefully we don’t have to worry about them.”

This comes as Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), The Hill’s polling partner, predicts Democrats will “likely” win the House, giving them an 83 percent chance of winning and Republicans a 17 percent chance.

In the Senate, DDHQ predicts Democrats have a 63 percent chance of regaining control, while Republicans were given a 37 percent chance.

Trump enjoyed a GOP-controlled Congress for the first two years of both of his terms, but Republicans lost control of the House in 2019. In that time, he threatened to veto multiple high-profile bills, including a Senate resolution blocking his declaration of a national emergency to build a wall on the Mexican border.

Other times the president used his veto pen was against previous war powers resolutions in 2020 related to the U.S. military’s assistance to Saudi Arabia in Yemen’s civil war and constraining his ability to take military action against Iran.

Democrats struggled to gain the two-thirds majority needed to override the president’s recent vetoes, with some suspecting that Trump rejected the bills in order to punish political enemies and act on his political grudges.

I still love the party.…
articles.body:
Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens (Mich.) defended her last-minute endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers in the battleground Michigan Senate race after initially supporting Democrat Abdul El-Sayed

“I’m not turning my back on Democrats,” she told reporters in Detroit alongside Rogers. “It is this one vote.”

“It’s my personal and private decision. I still love the party. I’ve done a ton for the party,” she continued. “I’ve voted for the party over and over and over again. I’m going to continue to do that as I fill out my term. Everyone should be fired up for Democrats.”

Stevens cited controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who El-Sayed campaigned with during the primary battle, as the reason why she decided to reverse course on her endorsement. El-Sayed has not appeared alongside Piker since he beat Stevens in the August Democratic primary.

“When you see us standing with Hasan Piker and repeated hate, it’s not acceptable,” she said. “That’s it.”

Rogers said Sunday that he was “honored” to have the Democrat’s support and called her endorsement an example of “courage in politics.”

Stevens shocked her party on Sunday when she attended service at Detroit’s Perfecting Church alongside Rogers, just two days out from Election Day.

A Decision Desk HQ polling average of Michigan Senate surveys shows El-Sayed leading Rogers by roughly 4 percentage points.

The congresswoman was previously invited to attend a Sunday campaign event with El-Sayed brokered by Democratic Reps. Jim Clyburn (S.C.) and Debbie Dingell (Mich.). However, the Democratic Senate nominee disinvited Stevens from the event after she took to social media to criticize El-Sayed on Friday — which she repeatedly cited Sunday when asked about her endorsement of Rogers.

“Abdul was very clear. He said, ‘Don’t come,’” Stevens said Sunday.

Stevens had pushed for El-Sayed to disavow an ad created by a group supporting the progressive that blamed high grocery prices on Israel and the war in Gaza. El-Sayed told MS NOW that his campaign was not behind the ad and that “I do not agree with the contents of that ad.”

A source familiar confirmed to NewsNation , The Hill’s sister network, on Saturday that El-Sayed disinvited her from the planned Sunday event and did not want her near his other campaign events.

The rift between El-Sayed and Stevens is unwelcome news for Democrats who need to hold onto retiring Sen. Gary Peters (D-Mich.) seat to flip the upper chamber. Democrats have sought to patch up party divisions after a nasty primary that largely focused on Israel, and Stevens, had indicated she would vote for El-Sayed until Sunday.

“I endorsed him. I meant it when I endorsed him,” she said Sunday of her initial support for El-Sayed after her narrow primary loss.

Sunday’s press gaggle ended abruptly after an attendee shouted that Stevens was a “traitor.”

Democrats have come out in defense of El-Sayed after Stevens’s Sunday reversal.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), the Senate Democrats’ campaign arm and Michigan Democrats released statements of their own underscoring that they were behind El-Sayed on Tuesday.

“The stakes of this election could not be higher: Mike Rogers is a rubber stamp for Donald Trump, and together they plan to continue sowing chaos and making life unaffordable for families while prioritizing their billionaire donors at the expense of Michigan families,” Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), chair of the Senate Democrats’ campaign arm, said in a statement.

“We stand firmly behind Abdul El-Sayed, who is a fighter for Michiganders and will work tirelessly to be the champion they need in the Senate, and we reject any efforts to divide Democrats ahead of Tuesday’s crucial election,” she added.

articles.title: Federal judge dismisses Trump attempt to interfere in Alaska Senate race
articles.summary: The president had requested that Alaska segregate ballots cast for a candidate with the same name as the incumbent. The judge said that would “violate Alaskans’ right to a secret ballot.”
articles.body: A federal judge in Alaska on Sunday dismissed the Trump administration’s lawsuit seeking to separate and preserve certain ballots in the state’s upcoming Senate election, where GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan faces Democrat Mary Peltola. In the last week, Peltola’s campaign has faced scrutiny after The New York Times reported the campaign and other Democrats recruited a candidate — Dan J. Sullivan — to run for the Senate with the same name as the incumbent senator. Citing potential voter confusion, the Trump administration sought to separate and preserve ballots with votes for Dan J. Sullivan, arguing that if the incumbent loses, it may be because people voted for the other Sullivan by mistake. In her ruling, U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason voiced concerns about voters’ right to a secret ballot. “The absence of any explanation from the United States as to how its requested relief could redress its alleged injury while simultaneously maintaining the secrecy of the ballot is telling,” Gleason wrote. Later, she added: “Requiring the segregation of ballots cast by voters for Daniel J. Sullivan so that these voters can be further investigated by law enforcement is not a remedy that this Court can or should order as it clearly violate Alaskans’ right to a secret ballot.” The lawsuit also sought to block the certification of the Senate election if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. On Saturday, the Republican-led state government in Alaska implored a federal judge to prevent that effort in a court filing. In response to the ruling, a spokesperson for Peltola’s campaign told NBC News, “No sham investigation or baseless lawsuit from a weaponized Department of Justice is going to stop Alaskans from electing Mary on November 3rd so she can lower costs for Alaska’s working families. Alaskans will choose their next U.S. Senator — not Dan Sullivan or his DC allies.” Shortly after the judge’s ruling, the Justice Department appealed. “The court dismissed the case on procedural grounds but did not dispute the argument of the United States that Daniel J. Sullivan (a/k/a Decoy Dan) entered the race as a frivolous candidate to confuse voters. DOJ plans to file a notice of appeal. Alaskan voters deserve a fair election, not to be misled in an attempt to rig outcomes,” a department spokesperson said. Republicans have criticized Dan J. Sullivan’s presence on the ballot for months, after he won a primary bid to be the fourth candidate on the general election ballot in August. The senator and his GOP allies long accused Democrats of recruiting the second Sullivan, a charge Peltola and her campaign have repeatedly denied. President Donald Trump accused Dan. J Sullivan of committing a “criminal act” Sunday on Truth Social. “The Fake Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr., has DISAPPEARED! Nobody can find him, including Law Enforcement. He knows that he committed a Criminal Act,” the president wrote. Last week, the Times report cited on-the-record comments from Peltola’s former campaign manager, who was fired in August, about the campaign’s efforts to recruit a second Dan Sullivan to run for office. The campaign manager and several unnamed sources said operatives from the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee joined the effort. Elisa Rios, the campaign manager who was fired, later sought to retract her comments. On Sunday, the senator called Democrats’ effort “rigged and corrupt” in a CNN interview. He added that no matter the outcome, “I’m going to accept the election results.”

Stevens shocked her party earlier on Sunday by reversing her endorsement of El-Sayed and instead backing the Michigan Senate GOP nominee and appearing alongside Rogers at a church event.

She pointed to El-Sayed’s decision to campaign earlier on with controversial far-left Twitch stream Hasan Piker and for disinviting her from a campaign event that was scheduled on Sunday.

Several aides from her official office, including her chief of staff, announced their resignations shortly after the move. Some of her former Senate campaign staff also took to social media to criticize her move.

Arik Wolk, who served as a spokesman for her Senate bid, called the developments on X “ridiculous and pathetic.”

Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), chair of the Senate Democrats’ campaign arm, said in a statement.

“We stand firmly behind Abdul El-Sayed, who is a fighter for Michiganders and will work tirelessly to be the champion they need in the Senate, and we reject any efforts to divide Democrats ahead of Tuesday’s crucial election,” she added.

articles.title: DNC chair defends El-Sayed, Peltola as Democrats brace for post-election legal fights
articles.summary: Democratic National Committee (DNC) Chair Ken Martin defended Democratic Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed and former Rep. Mary Peltola (D-Alaska) against recent GOP attacks amid growing concern the party will have to brace for post-election legal fights. “What Dr. El-Sayed has said is true. I mean, what most Michiganders care about is not all of this…
articles.body:
Democratic National Committee (DNC) Chair Ken Martin defended Democratic Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed and former Rep. Mary Peltola (D-Alaska) against recent GOP attacks amid growing concern the party will have to brace for post-election legal fights .

“What Dr. El-Sayed has said is true. I mean, what most Michiganders care about is not all of this controversy that’s swirling around right now. What they’re focused on is the fact that they can barely afford their lives right now,” Martin said during an appearance on “The Hill Sunday.”

El-Sayed has been called out by former primary opponent Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) over recent ads aired by a super PAC supporting his campaign that tied rising grocery prices to U.S. military aid to Israel.

Martin similarly called Stevens’s recent decision to endorse former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) in the state’s competitive Senate race “disappointing” and a “political stunt.”

Peltola is facing her own challenges as the GOP launched multiple probes into her campaign following a New York Times report alleging she participated in a “ballot-stacking” scheme to recruit another candidate who shared the same name as incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska).

Ballot “stacking” is a common practice, especially in Alaska’s unusual nonpartisan, top four voting system. GOP strategists previously told The Hill that it is not illegal.

“I’m certainly uncomfortable with any of those types of tactics. But let me say, Mary Peltola has made it very clear that she had nothing to do with this, nor anyone on her campaign,” Martin stated. “But the reality is the Supreme Court in Alaska has already decided in this case. This was brought earlier this year, as you know. They said that it’s fine to have two Dan Sullivans on the ballot, but that they needed to make sure that there was no voter confusion.”

The DNC chair is referring to a recent decision that listed the senator as “incumbent” and “Registered Republican” on ballots, while the other candidate was listed as “Sullivan, Daniel J. Jr.” “A lot of Alaskans have already voted, and they’re voting for Mary Peltola,” Martin concluded. “Dan Sullivan, the current incumbent, had an opportunity in the Senate to actually deliver for Alaskans. He chose not to.”

A federal judge dismissed the Trump administration’s lawsuit in Alaska that sought to block certification if the second Dan Sullivan running for Senate causes voter confusion.

The House Oversight Committee’s probe into the matter is still ongoing. Rep. James Comer (R-Ky.) warned there’s “a big possibility” Peltola will not be seated even if she won the race.

articles.body:
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) ripped Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) over her eleventh hour endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers in the competitive Michigan Senate contest.

“This is a despicable betrayal from Rep. Stevens,” Schumer wrote Sunday on the social platform X, reiterating his support for Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in the race.

Schumer’s remarks are particularly notable because he backed Stevens in the nasty Democratic primary against El-Sayed. The Senate Democrat threw his support behind El-Sayed after he narrowly beat Stevens in August.

“Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors,” the New York Democrat said.

Stevens shocked Democrats Sunday when she appeared alongside Rogers, a former House Republican, at a church in Detroit and issued an endorsement. She previously called Rogers a “rubber stamp” for President Trump.

“As you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign, and that I should stay away. And he’s right,” she said in a video posted to social media Sunday. “And that’s why I am endorsing my Rogers for the United States Senate today.”

Stevens was initially set to attend a campaign event alongside El-Sayed with Rep. Jim Clyburn (D-S.C.) on Sunday, but the Senate Democratic nominee disinvited her from the event amid heightened tensions between the pair.

Stevens, on Friday, took to social media to say she would appear alongisde El-Sayed for the first time since her primary loss at the Sunday event, but expected an apology from him over his response to a controversial ad. El-Sayed accused Stevens of relitigating their primary .

Schumer joins a chorus of other Democrats that have criticized Stevens over her newfound support for Rogers.

“Congresswoman Stevens is not a current member of the Michigan Democratic Party, nor will she be in the future,” Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel wrote on X Sunday.

Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D) also condemned Stevens’s endorsement.

“Anyone who makes an election this important about themselves, and not Michiganders and our democracy, should think hard about whether they are serving the greater good,” she wrote on social media.

Stevens endorsed Rogers over Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (D), who Stevens lost to after a bitter primary battle. She had endorsed El-Sayed earlier this year after that loss but did not campaign with the nominee.

She was set to appear alongside El-Sayed on Sunday, but the Democratic nominee dropped Stevens from the campaign event, according to sources familiar with the matter.

Democrats looking to hold on to the seat that’s to be vacated by outgoing Sen. Gary Peters (D) –– and seeking to make a net gain of four seats to take a majority in the Senate –– fumed over her endorsement.

“Haley Stevens’ decision to campaign with Rogers — a man who has repeatedly sold out Michigan’s working class, wants to pass a national abortion ban, and has pledged to be a loyal vote for Trump’s agenda — shows that she has abandoned everything she claims to care about,” Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel said in a statement.

El-Sayed dismissed Stevens’s move during a campaign event flanked by Sen. Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.) and Rep. James Clyburn (D-S.C.), on Sunday in Detroit.

“This is a state of 10 million people who deserve a lot better from the government,” he said. “I’m a lot more focused on the 9,999,998 that are not the ones you guys are talking about.”

Steven and El-Sayed have been at odds with each other over U.S. support for Israel. This divide represents the larger divide among Democrats over the issue, with many not approving of Israel’s actions during its war in Gaza, and many others accusing Israel of committing genocide in the territory.

articles.title: Why did Democrat Haley Stevens just endorse a Republican for US Senate?
articles.summary: Stevens’s endorsement of Mike Rogers comes after a bitter dispute with Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed.
articles.body:
A Democratic congresswoman has thrown her support behind a Republican in one of the most closely watched races of the US midterm elections, just two days before voters head to the polls.

Haley Stevens, who lost Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary in August, announced on Sunday that she was endorsing Republican Mike Rogers over her own party’s nominee, Abdul El-Sayed.

The decision follows weeks of tension between the two Democrats over Israel and has provoked a backlash within the party as it fights to win control of Congress and limit President Donald Trump’s power.

Stevens is a Democratic congresswoman from Michigan who narrowly lost the party’s Senate primary to El-Sayed, a former public health official who could become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

Despite a bitter primary battle, Stevens promised to support El-Sayed and said as recently as Wednesday that she still wanted him to win.

That was despite her fiance, Jason Turkish, a Jewish Democrat and civil rights lawyer, announcing that he would vote for Rogers. Turkish – who, according to Federal Election Commission (FEC) reports, has donated nearly $250,000 to both Democrats and Republicans during this midterm cycle – accused El-Sayed of anti-Semitism, saying his rhetoric about Israel and its war in Gaza had made Jewish voters feel unsafe.

And on Sunday, Stevens changed her position.

Why did Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers?

The decision followed weeks of tension over Israel that became increasingly public in the final days of the campaign.

Stevens is a strong supporter of Israel, while El-Sayed has been an outspoken critic of Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza and US military aid to the country.

Their differences were also a major issue during the Democratic primary, when a super PAC affiliated with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) spent tens of millions of dollars to back Stevens.

But the latest dispute began last week, when an independent group backing El-Sayed, Rebellion PAC, released an advertisement linking US military aid to Israel to Americans’ struggles with the cost of living.

The advertisement shows a couple shopping for groceries who decide to put back a carton of eggs because they need to save that money for “killing Palestinians”.

Stevens called the advertisement anti-Semitic and demanded that El-Sayed condemn it. She also accused him of making similar arguments as in the ad by suggesting that money spent on Israel could instead go towards schools, healthcare and childcare.

El-Sayed said the advertisement was not produced by his campaign and that he disagreed with its message, adding that Stevens was trying to re-litigate their primary rather than focusing on defeating Rogers.

The tensions came to a head on Sunday, when Stevens and El-Sayed were supposed to attend a church service together in a show of Democratic unity, but Stevens was uninvited.

“Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away,” she said in a video on X, announcing she was going to endorse Rogers.

“And he’s right. And that’s why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today.”

But Democratic Congresswoman Debbie Dingell, who helped organise the event, said she was the one who asked Stevens not to attend, telling The Associated Press news agency that “it had become way too distracting”.

Stevens also criticised El-Sayed’s association with political streamer Hasan Piker, whose uncle, Cenk Uygur, founded the PAC that released the advertisement.

Stevens told reporters on Sunday, with Rogers standing beside her: “We can’t stand with hate. We can’t stand with Hasan Piker.”

She insisted she was still a Democrat and planned to vote for Democratic candidates in 90 percent of the races on her ballot, but her Senate vote would go to Rogers.

Her decision has drawn an angry response from Democrats, including some of the party’s most senior figures.

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer called the endorsement a “despicable betrayal”, saying Senate Democrats remained united behind El-Sayed.

He brushed off questions about whether Stevens had betrayed the Democratic Party, saying he was more concerned about the issues facing Michigan voters.

“At the end of the day, I actually don’t think about Haley Stevens,” he told reporters. “I’m just less interested in the politics of it all than I am in the policy of it all.”

He urged voters to focus instead on healthcare, civil rights and the differences between his campaign and that of Rogers, who is backed by Trump.

The Democratic National Committee (DNC) issued a blistering statement in response to Stevens’s “last-minute political stunts”.

“Haley Stevens’ disappointing decision to endorse Mike Rogers, a Trump ally who would join Republican efforts to sell out working families, is a betrayal of the values of the Democratic Party,” DNC Chair Ken Martin said.

“At a moment when Democrats are united in fighting for Michigan families and standing up to Trump’s agenda, we reject these efforts to sow division within our party.”

The local arm of the DNC, the Michigan Democratic Party (MDP), also had strong words for Haley’s endorsement of Rogers.

“Haley Stevens’ decision to campaign with Rogers … shows that she has abandoned everything she claims to care about,” MDP Chair Curtis Hertel said. “We reject the attempts by Stevens and bad-faith actors to divide our party and undermine our momentum, and will not allow these eleventh-hour distractions deter us.”

Stevens’s decision also prompted resignations within her own team. Her chief of staff for eight years, Justin German, announced that he and several other staff members had stepped down over the endorsement.

“We are shocked and heartbroken by Congresswoman Stevens’s decision to support Mike Rogers,” German said in a statement first shared by CNN.

Trump, meanwhile, celebrated her decision.

“Wow, this is BIG!” he wrote in a social media post on Sunday.

During a rally in Iowa later in the day, the president said he would “love” if Stevens joined the Republican Party.

“Haley said what few people are willing to say,” Trump added. “It’s a thing called bravery.”

Republican House of Representatives Speaker Mike Johnson, who flew with Trump to Iowa, also celebrated Stevens, telling reporters he sent the congresswoman a note after her “courageous” endorsement.

“Haley’s a good person. She’s always been very thoughtful”, Johnson said, describing Michigan’s Senate race as a “contrast” election. “She loves her state. She’s served it as best she could. She’s speaking the truth.”

Could Stevens’s endorsement affect the Michigan Senate race?

El-Sayed and Rogers are competing to replace retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters in a closely contested race that could help determine which party controls the US Senate.

Republicans currently control both chambers of Congress, and Democrats are hoping to win enough seats to challenge Trump’s agenda and increase scrutiny of his administration.

Stevens defeated El-Sayed in Wayne County, which includes Detroit, and neighbouring Oakland County, drawing support from Black and Jewish Democratic voters. Both counties are Democratic strongholds, where turnout could help determine Tuesday’s result.

The question now is whether Stevens’s endorsement could convince some of her supporters to back Rogers, or discourage them from voting altogether.

Polling suggests El-Sayed has largely consolidated Democratic support, according to the Reuters news agency.

Early voting began on October 24, before the latest dispute erupted.

articles.title: Trump is giving his closing midterm pitch at problem-plagued Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump is making his closing pitch of the midterm elections at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, pushing his slow, expe...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump is making his closing pitch of the midterm elections at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool , pushing his slow, expensive and problem-plagued efforts to repair it back into the spotlight on the eve of Election Day .

In comments to reporters as he deplaned from Air Force One for a Sunday rally in Iowa, Trump said his speaking at the site would "show how beautiful it is."

"We might hold it tomorrow or something," the president added, without giving specifics. Hours later, the White House formally announced he'd be giving a speech there Monday afternoon.

Rather than using Monday to travel to key states and try to energize his "Make America Great Again" supporters as his Republican Party tries to maintain control of Congress, Trump opted for an event at a Washington renovation project that has been embarrassing and contentious.

The unusual move marks a departure from Trump's month-long race to stage more than 25 rallies in largely conservative areas, hoping the GOP can overcome his own low approval ratings and polls predicting that the Iran war , high energy prices and cost of living increases could spell a strong election night for Democrats .

Trump wrote on his social media site that his Sunday evening rally in Kansas — which followed his Iowa visit — was "my last stop."

The presidewnt spent a lot of time at those rallies talking about his second-term focus on molding the White House and the surrounding nation's capital in his own image. He crammed the Oval Office with gold flourishes , demolishing the East Wing to construct a sprawling ballroom , converting the Rose Garden into a patio space reminiscent of his Mar-a-Lago estate and erecting a sprawling South Lawn helipad.

Trump also closed the Kennedy Center after failed attempts to add his name to the building , has planned a towering arch just outside the city and is pushing to revamp a century-old public golf course .

He has bristled at criticisms from former President Barack Obama and other Democrats that he's spent too much time focused on construction projects — insisting that renovations relax him and that he does them quickly and without requiring too much planning time.

Trump said the Reflecting Pool fix would be fast and inexpensive

His Reflecting Pool saga began in April when Trump said he wanted to change its color and would use contractors he knew to fix the monument in mere days and for about $1.5 million before Independence Day.

The repairs wrapped up nearly three months behind schedule and the budget ballooned to more than 10 times Trump's early estimate — and that's assuming no more additional work will need to be done in the future.

Trump had initially declared the work was complete in June. But after unveiling the overhaul, the pool was soon choked with algae blooms , and its "American-flag blue" liner began peeling off in sections. The pool was quickly drained anew for repairs in mid-July.

Trump has repeatedly blamed vandals, but the office of U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia — former Fox News host and longtime Trump ally Jeanine Pirro — said the problems were caused by shoddy workmanship .

In his comments Sunday, Trump continued to insist that the Reflecting Pool "was vandalized badly." He said that security cameras have since been added to stop that.

Still, a particularly ignominious moment came when the Justice Department charged former Olympian David Hearn with intentionally damaging the Reflecting Pool — then abruptly dropped the case this summer — determining he was not responsible.

That prompted Trump to fume that Pirro "choked," and that he was "disappointed with Jeanine Pirro, really disappointed. She folded like an umbrella" — though he stopped short of firing her.

articles.title: El Sayed's left-wing allies attack 'evil' Stevens after bombshell Rogers endorsement
articles.summary: Hasan Piker, Mehdi Hasan and others attacked Haley Stevens on X after she surprisingly endorsed Republican Mike Rogers in the heated Michigan Senate race.
articles.body: Left-wing allies of Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed erupted Sunday after the stunning decision by Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens to endorse his Republican rival Mike Rogers. Stevens, who narrowly lost in the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, has been critical of his unwillingness to condemn the overt antisemitism of some of his supporters. After recent barbs between the two, El-Sayed disinvited her from a campaign event meant to showcase party unity in the critical Senate race, before she then endorsed his GOP opponent in a surprising last-second decision. Far-left streamer Hasan Piker attacked her motives in a post to X, claiming she was "weirdly obsessed with Israel." "haley stevens is not the spokesperson for democrats, she’s not the spox for jewish people or black people," Piker said on X. "she’s a self interested striver who’s weirdly obsessed with israel and has been paid handsomely for this strange obsession. this race is about solving the affordability crisis, defending democracy, fighting back against the racialized violence all communities have faced since trump came into power and serving michigan. haley and mike rogers serve trump, and trump serves the epstein class. the choice is clear." DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS ENDORSES GOP SENATE NOMINEE MIKE ROGERS AT DETROIT CHURCH "She’s clearly a disturbed, deranged, dishonest woman (less than 48 hours ago she was swearing to the NYT she was backing Abdul)," Zeteo News' editor-in-chief Mehdi Hasan also said on X, going on to attack the Democratic establishment for putting forward a "complete traitor." In another post agreeing with Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen accusing Stevens of being used as a "tool" for "racism and religious bigotry," Hasan said "Islamophobia" was "at the core" of her endorsement. Hasan also questioned Democratic leaders’ support for Stevens, writing, "She's evil." Former DNC Vice Chair David Hogg also attacked Stevens and urged Democrats to denounce the congresswoman, who has said she remains a proud Democrat. "If you supported Haley Stevens now is your time to speak out, denounce her as the Republican she is and apologize for supporting a traitor," Hogg wrote. ABDUL EL-SAYED PLAYS DOWN HASAN PIKER TIES AFTER STREAMER’S VIRAL ANTISEMITISM FIRESTORM The endorsement followed a controversial ad put up by Rebellion PAC, founded by The Young Turks host Cenk Uygur, in support of El-Sayed's campaign. The ad depicted grocery shoppers blaming U.S. military support for Israel for high grocery prices. Stevens called the ad antisemitic and demanded El-Sayed condemn it. His campaign said it was not affiliated with the ad, and he subsequently said he disagreed with its contents. Uygur defended the Rebellion PAC's advertisement before the endorsement, disputing claims that it blamed Jewish people for grocery prices. He said the spot concerned Israel and accused reporters of misrepresenting the message. On Sunday, Uygur claimed Stevens endorsed Rogers because "her only source of power is the Israeli lobby" and "She has no popular support, just AIPAC money." Former Obama aides and "Pod Save America" co-hosts Jon Lovett and Tommy Vietor also criticized Stevens for backing Rogers. "So [Stevens] didn’t feel welcome at a political event, so now she doesn’t care if Democrats win the Senate," Lovett wrote. "She’s against ‘hate’ while supporting one of the most hateful campaigns in memory. She endorsed then unendorsed then endorsed then unendorsed her former rival, who she promised to unite behind, after endlessly repeating (correctly!) that Mike Rogers MUST be defeated. What an incoherent disgrace. Hope this anger drives people to do whatever they can to help [El-Sayed] win." Vietor also wrote, "I hope folks will think about the fact that [Stevens] demanded that [El-Sayed] denounce as antisemitic an ad he was not associated with, but is now endorsing a man who called Abdul a terrorist. She is fine with bigotry and racism as long as its against the right people." EL-SAYED DISTANCES HIMSELF FROM HASAN PIKER AFTER DISTURBING REMARKS ABOUT JEWISH AMERICANS El-Sayed previously addressed the ad controversy, saying his campaign did not produce the Rebellion PAC advertisement and that he disagreed with its contents. "You guys love to play the condemn game. I've already been clear that that ad was not made by me, and I do not agree with the contents of that ad," El-Sayed said in a campaign press gaggle Saturday. The Republican National Committee welcomed Stevens’ decision. In a statement provided to Fox News Digital, RNC spokesman Hunter Lovell said the endorsement demonstrated Rogers’ appeal beyond Republican voters. "When Congresswoman Haley Stevens, who ran against Abdul El-Sayed and knows him better than anyone, stands with Mike Rogers, Michigan should take notice," Lovell said. "Democrats who feel Abdul has abandoned them have a home with Mike, who is building a winning coalition of Democrats, Independents, and Republicans to save Michigan from El-Sayed's radical, terrorist-sympathizing agenda. The center of Michigan politics has moved, and Abdul is on the wrong side of it." ROGERS WARNS MICHIGAN VOTERS AGAINST EL-SAYED’S ‘EXTREME’ AGENDA AHEAD OF ELECTION Journalist Sam Robinson asked Stevenson Sunday how she could support a candidate whose positions directly opposed hers. "Nothing is perfect," Stevens said. The video shows a heckler interrupting Robinson, ending the exchange. "Stevens is a traitor," the heckler said. Stevens’ fiancé, Jason Turkish, and former campaign chairman David Kramer had already decided to vote for Rogers, Fox News Digital reported. articles.title: Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit over two Dan Sullivans in Alaska election
articles.summary: The Department of Justice had sought to delay certifying results in Alaska's crucial Senate race if the Republican incumbent loses.
articles.body:
A judge has tossed a lawsuit by the Trump administration that sought to delay certifying results in Alaska's crucial Senate race if the Republican incumbent loses.

The suit by the US Department of Justice argued that having two candidates named Dan Sullivan on the ballot could cause "voter confusion" and take support from incumbent Republican Dan S Sullivan.

The judge ruled that the federal government doesn't have authority to force Alaska to segregate and investigate any ballots in the three-way race between Sullivan, Daniel J Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola.

The Alaska Senate contest is considered one the closest in the Tuesday midterms, where control of Congress will be up for grabs.

"The United States provides no workable plan as to how it proposes to segregate ballots cast for Daniel J. Sullivan on Election Day and then conduct a court-ordered unspecified 'investigation' of those ballots in a manner that would preserve voter secrecy," US District Judge Sharon Gleason wrote in the ruling.

Alaska voters have the right to a secret ballot, she wrote, adding that regardless, such a move by the justice department would be too late as it is only days before the midterm election. Many voters have already cast their ballots in early voting and postal voting.

After the ruling, the justice department said it would file to appeal. It said in a statement that the court dismissed the federal case on "procedural grounds but did not dispute the argument of the United States that Daniel J. Sullivan (a/k/a Decoy Dan) entered the race as a frivolous candidate to confuse voters".

"Alaskan voters deserve a fair election, not to be misled in an attempt to rig outcomes," the statement continued.

Asked about the lawsuit last month, President Donald Trump said he had directed the justice department to file it.

"All of a sudden he decides to run for the Senate, and his name is Dan Sullivan. One is Daniel S., one is Daniel J. The Daniel J. is the fake," Trump told reporters.

Daniel J Sullivan, the little-known candidate running with no party affiliation, had previously told The New York Times he has voted both Democrat and Republican in the past.

Senator Dan S Sullivan, the incumbent Republican, and his allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters.

Then last week, controversy erupted when The New York Times reported that Democrats on Peltola's team worked with people who tried to recruit spoiler candidates in the Senate race.

Peltola has denied she knowing anything about an alleged "scheme" that led to the two Dan Sullivans standing in the race.

The Alaska race is considered by analysts to be one of the tightest in the upcoming US midterm elections, which will decide which party controls Congress for the last two years of Trump's presidency.

articles.title: Why governors’ races are important in the 2026 US midterms
articles.summary: Historic turnover in this election will allow dozens of states to vote on significant changes in leadership.
articles.body:
Much of the attention ahead of Tuesday’s midterm elections has fallen on the battle for control of the United States Congress.

But key state-level races are also unfolding, with far-reaching consequences for the country’s future.

This year, 36 US states will vote for their next governor, the most powerful elected official in state government.

An unusually high proportion of those races centre on open seats, with no incumbent governor on the ballot seeking re-election.

In 19 of the races, the current officeholder is either term-limited, like California Democrat Gavin Newsom , or voluntarily opted to not run again, like Iowa Republican Kim Reynolds.

This historic turnover creates the potential for several states to take on significant changes in leadership.

Governors serve as the chief executives of their states, overseeing government departments and agencies responsible for delivering public services.

Their powers vary by state. In general, governors propose budgets, appoint senior state officials, direct state agencies about how to enforce existing law, and issue executive orders.

They can also choose to sign into law bills passed by their state’s legislature — or veto them.

One of their most visible areas of influence is reproductive rights. Since the US Supreme Court ruled in 2022 that there is no constitutional right to abortion access, state governments have played a central role in determining whether the procedure is legal.

Each state can now regulate abortion within its boundaries, and some 13 state legislatures have passed complete or near-total abortion bans.

But the Guttmacher Institute, a US-based reproductive rights organisation, noted that about a dozen governors have issued executive orders to “mitigate” the harm done by such bans.

“By issuing executive orders, governors could quickly declare immediate protections for providers and patients,” the organisation said. “This was particularly helpful in states such as North Carolina, where the governor is supportive of abortion rights — but the legislature is not.”

Governors can also influence how US elections are administered.

In some states, governors appoint the officials responsible for overseeing elections, while in others, those officials are elected independently. Governors may also sign or veto legislation changing voting rules, giving them significant influence over election administration.

Governors also help shape how states respond to the federal government.

They may challenge federal policies in court or negotiate with Washington over funding and programme requirements.

State governments also play a major role in implementing federally funded programmes, making cooperation between governors and the White House important.

One example came after former US President Barack Obama’s landmark healthcare policy, the Affordable Care Act, passed the US Congress in 2010.

In the aftermath of its passage, many governors were in a position to decide whether their states adopted the Affordable Care Act’s expansion to Medicaid, an insurance programme for low-income households.

Some governors, like Steve Beshear of Kentucky and Earl Ray Tomblin of West Virginia, issued executive orders in 2013 to adopt Medicaid expansion without their legislatures’ approval.

Others, like Florida’s then-Governor Rick Scott, opposed Medicaid expansion and directed their state legislatures not to adopt it. Scott, who now serves as a US senator for the state, later dropped his opposition, but the Republican-led Florida legislature did not take up a bill to agree to the expansion.

As their state’s chief executives, governors have a unique platform to showcase their political talents.

Many use the governor’s mansion to catapult to the nation’s highest office, the presidency.

At least 17 former US presidents – including Jimmy Carter, Ronald Reagan, Bill Clinton and George W Bush – were governors before they occupied the White House.

But some governors find their presidential ambitions thwarted by backlash to their state-level policies.

The Eagleton Institute of Politics estimates that only 53 percent of the presidential nominees who were previously governors were ultimately victorious in their races.

During the 2016 presidential election cycle, for instance, the governor of New Jersey at the time, Chris Christie, hoped to secure the Republican Party’s nomination.

He dropped out of the race in February of that year, however, amid criticism of several actions undertaken during his governorship.

His administration in New Jersey was still reeling from a scandal known as “Bridgegate”, which concerned accusations that a major roadway was closed to punish the mayor of a nearby city.

And some Republicans denounced the way Christie had greeted Obama, a Democrat, when he visited New Jersey during Hurricane Sandy in October 2012.

This year’s midterm races are expected to set the stage for the presidential election in 2028.

Several outgoing governors are among the likely hopefuls. Newsom, who has served as California’s governor since 2019, is prevented from running for a third term this year.

Instead, he is widely speculated to be a frontrunner for the Democratic nomination in 2028, having established himself as a vocal critic of Republican President Donald Trump.

Several other potential Democratic contenders are also locked in re-election campaigns this midterm cycle that could serve as previews for future presidential bids. They include Wes Moore of Maryland and Josh Shapiro of Pennsylvania.

articles.title: Presidência do Senado: PL deve ter candidato próprio, mesmo com aproximação de Alcolumbre | G1
articles.standfirst: Senadores escolhem em fevereiro de 2027 quem comandará a Casa pelos próximos dois anos. Atual presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) tenta se reeleger ao cargo.
articles.summary: Senadores escolhem em fevereiro de 2027 quem comandará a Casa pelos próximos dois anos. Atual presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) tenta se reeleger ao cargo.
articles.body:
Apesar das tratativas do presidente do Senado , Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), com senadores de todos os partidos, o PL deve anunciar, na próxima quarta-feira (4), Rogério Marinho (RN) como candidato à presidência do Senado em fevereiro de 2027.

O partido terá a maior bancada do Senado a partir dos novos senadores, eleitos em outubro . Serão 28 parlamentares.

Alcolumbre tenta se reeleger ao cargo. A estratégia do amapaense passa por conseguir votos mesmo de senadores de partidos da oposição, como PL, PP e Republicanos.

🔎 Para ser eleito, o candidato à presidência do Senado precisa conquistar a maioria absoluta dos votos, ou seja, 41 de 80 votos.

Desta forma, o presidente do Senado poderia angariar apoio da oposição para uma eventual reeleição e ainda conter a pressão por impeachment de ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

O último levantamento do STF, de abril, informa que, dos condenados pela tentativa de golpe, há ainda 190 presos . Desses, 70 estão em prisão domiciliar.

Em abril desde ano, o Congresso deu aval a uma proposta que permite a redução das penas, que será avaliada caso a caso pelo STF.

Uma liderança importante do PL dentro do Senado afirmou, nos bastidores, que essa tese da anistia poderia servir tanto para os condenados quanto para quem os julgou, em referência ao relator do caso, ministro Alexandre de Moraes.

Desta forma, uma apuração relativa à conduta do ministro na condução do processo não seria aberta pelo Senado.

Esse senador também afirmou que defendeu, para os colegas de partido, que talvez não valha para o PL o "desgaste" de apostar numa candidatura própria para disputar a presidência do Senado e, em caso de derrota, a legenda ficar sem o comando de comissões importantes. A exemplo do que aconteceu em 2023, quando Rogério Marinho, candidato pelo PL, foi derrotado por Rodrigo Pacheco.

O parlamentar do PL argumenta ser contrário a uma "radicalização" na eleição da Mesa, ou seja, que o PL lance candidato sem antes tentar compor um acordo com Alcolumbre.

Mesmo com a tentativa de aproximação, o PL, de forma majoritária, não aceitou um acordo com o presidente do Senado e pretende colocar Marinho em campanha a partir da próxima semana.

Senador Rogério Marinho (PL-RN) e Presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) — Foto: Carlos Moura/Agência Senado

“A candidatura com mais força e votos hoje é a de Rogério Marinho”, afirmou o senador eleito Carlos Jordy (PL-RJ).

Além de Marinho, a senadora Tereza Cristina (PP-MS) é outro quadro da oposição que deseja disputar o comando da Casa.

Mesmo com o PL lançando Rogério Marinho, Tereza mantém o desejo de concorrer à presidência do Senado. “Eu mantenho meu desejo de concorrer, de ser a primeira mulher presidente do Senado. Temos 90 dias até a eleição. Tem muita água pra rolar”, declarou Tereza ao g1.

Entre os parlamentares de oposição, há uma avaliação de que a carta escrita pelo senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) em que se autodeclarou “presidente eleito” e depois mudou para líder do Brasil, enfraqueceu a candidatura de Rogério Marinho.

Senadores acreditam que Marinho, que foi coordenador da campanha de Flávio à presidência da República, comandaria o Senado sem autoridade e “precisando ligar para os Estados Unidos” para definir o rumo da Casa.

Na quarta-feira (28), Marinho confirmou que deverá ser o candidato da legenda.

Neste mesmo dia, quando questionado sobre a carta redigida por Flávio Bolsonaro, Alcolumbre sinalizou esta aproximação que tenta com o grupo de oposicionistas : "Eu estou falando todo dia de pacificação do Brasil. Tudo que eu comentar para vocês pode ser contrário à minha tese", disse.

Um interlocutor do presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), avaliou que o amapaense já reúne os votos suficientes para sua reeleição , ou seja, ao menos 41 e que, diante da fuga de Flávio Bolsonaro do país , Marinho virou o candidato ideal para enfrentar em fevereiro.

Esse interlocutor confirmou que ele já possui votos dentro do próprio PL, mas ponderou que o presidente do Senado ainda não dialogou com a ala dita mais "radical" do bolsonarismo, composta pelos senadores eleitos como Guilherme Derrite (PP-SP) e Carol de Toni (PL-SC).

Além disso, afirmou que Alcolumbre ainda espera conversar nas próximas semanas com a senadora eleita pelo Distrito Federal, Michelle Bolsonaro (PL), que hoje apoia a candidatura de Tereza Cristina.

Apesar de alguns governistas, como o senador Otto Alencar (PSD-BA), defenderem o projeto de anistia , siglas como o MDB já estão se posicionando contra essa possibilidade.

articles.title: Democrats have high hopes for midterms, but polls have let them down before
articles.summary: Polls have been predicting a Democratic surge, but last-minute deciders and sampling issues mean there's no guarantee.
articles.body:
The Democratic Party has high expectations as it heads into these pivotal US midterm elections.

A historically unpopular Republican president, an American public unhappy with the rising costs of food and bills, and months of favourable polls point to a good night for them on Tuesday.

Democratic candidates lead in well over the 218 seats needed to flip control of the lower chamber of Congress, the House of Representatives, the polls suggest. And they are tied or narrowly ahead in the key Senate races.

A recent New York Times poll had the Senate race in South Carolina, a state Donald Trump won by 18 percentage points in 2024, as a tie. Recent CNN surveys put the Democrats ahead in Texas, Kansas and Maine.

Recent US political history is littered with examples where public opinion polls, even ones just days before an election, were off the mark. Trump outperformed predictions on his way to White House victories in 2016 and 2024. His narrow defeat in 2020 came after most surveys indicated a more comfortable win for Democrat Joe Biden.

Earlier this year, polls suggested Democrat Abdul El-Sayed was poised for a double-digit win in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary. Instead it was 1%. In Wisconsin's Democratic primary for governor, the candidate that had a polling lead that approached 20 points lost by a fraction of a percent.

Democrats have an identity crisis - it won't be an easy fix

According to Clifford Young, president of Ipsos Public Affairs, which conducts political and market research surveys, polling has become difficult in recent years because it's harder to reach Americans as they abandon their land lines and screen their calls. And many of those who pollsters do contact have become less willing to participate.

"Conservatives, especially those on the far right, are much more anti-establishment by nature," Young says. "And they don't participate in anything. They hate the system. That's the challenge."

If Republican voters are being undercounted in a systematic way, and polling companies don't take that into consideration when constructing their voting models, it could skew their data towards the Democrats.

That's one of the reasons why it has become trickier for pollsters to predict what the electorate will look like.

One explanation for why Trump overperformed in previous presidential elections is that his supporters – many of whom were not regular voters – flocked to the polls in higher-than-expected numbers.

That unpredictability is one of the main contributing factors to those notable recent polling misses, even if the margins in most reputable polls were only off by a few percentage points.

In a close race, those few points can make the difference between victory and defeat for a candidate. And this year, many of the key Senate races are within those narrow margins.

In recent years, midterm general election polls have proven to be more accurate, in part because Trump - and his unique ability to draw disaffected Americans to the polls - was not on the ballot.

In 2022, they suggested Democrats would defy conventional expectations and avoid an electoral wipe-out despite Biden's low approval numbers.

While the party lost control of the House of Representatives, the margins were slim and Democrats maintained control of the US Senate.

While this year's primary results did provide bigger surprises, Young says that nominating contests have historically been volatile, with voters more likely to make up their minds at the last minute. It shouldn't be seen as an indication that the current crop of general election polls are off the mark.

It's common for the party of the president to have a bad night in the midterms.

One of the most notable examples in recent years came in 2010 when Republicans flipped more than 60 House seats and made gains in the Senate.

It came off the back of an economy struggling to recover from the financial crash and conservative fears over President Barack Obama's healthcare reforms. A defeat had been predicted by the polls but not quite on that scale.

The roles are reversed this time, with the Democrats in opposition and the economy on the minds of voters. But there are a number of reasons why Democrats may not have as good a night as history might suggest or as some might expect, given Trump's low approval rating.

Firstly, much of the territory in play in this election Trump conquered with ease in the presidential election just two years ago. It's like a home game for Republicans.

Then there have been changes to House election boundaries over the years that have meant fewer seats switch between parties.

Thirdly, there are fewer swing voters due to the deeper polarisation of the country. Some experts describe the electorate as calcified.

There's also the cash advantage Republicans have enjoyed which has given them hundreds of millions of dollars to spend on attack ads in the final weeks.

Polling models try to capture shifting fundamentals. And a well-designed poll is built to anticipate issues that may make it less than reliable.

Individual polls do have a built-in margin of error – a statistical level of uncertainty based on the sampling size compared to the population as a whole. Taken as an aggregate, polling averages and not individual surveys can provide a more accurate prediction.

At the moment, even the kind of polling lean we saw in recent presidential elections would suggest Democrats are likely to have a good night on 3 November. And polling inaccuracies can go both ways. In last year's state and special elections, Democrats outperformed most surveys as it was their voters who turned out in unexpectedly larger numbers.

The sight of Trump holding rallies in the final days of the campaign in states he won comfortably in 2024 will have lifted Democrats' hopes that Republican internal polling has conservative candidates in trouble.

There's always the chance that voters change their minds right up until election day, however.

Sometimes there are late shifts that can alter the dynamics of a race. Sometimes undecided voters, which still account for a key segment of the electorate in many of these races, all break the same way.

In polling, there will always be some level of uncertainty – and managing that is the art that goes along with the science.

"I think we're doing a better job," says Young. "But part of the problem we always have is not just with the pollsters. Part of it is that we're dealing with humans. Humans are not easy."
